title_candidates: This browser tool spots AI writing clichés
Find formulaic AI phrases before you publish
summary: Simon Willison's free browser tool flags formulaic phrases often associated with AI writing, with adjustable patterns and a paste-first workflow.

primary_source.title: LLM cliché highlighter
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: The browser-based analyzer flags clichéd phrases commonly associated with language-model writing.
Users can paste text into the tool or load a public URL for analysis.
Its pattern checks can be toggled, and matches appear within their surrounding sentences.
Willison created the app after repeatedly encountering formulaic constructions in AI-assisted writing; it initially targeted ten recurring patterns.

quote_candidates.text: Detect and highlight common clichéd phrases in text that frequently appear in language model outputs.

supporting_sources.title: LLM cliché highlighter
key_facts: The live tool supports pasted text, a built-in example, adjustable detectors, match navigation, and public URL loading.

supporting_sources.title: tools.simonwillison.net colophon — llm-cliche-highlighter
key_facts: The development log links the source code and records additions including local storage, URL loading, and more cliché patterns.

prerequisites: A paragraph to check, or a public article URL

steps.instruction: Open the highlighter and paste text into the main box; analysis runs as you type.
Select 'Load example' and confirm the summary and highlighted-text sections populate.
Expand 'Patterns' and toggle detectors; confirm the match count or highlights change.
Hover a highlight to identify its rule, then review every flagged phrase in the Matches list.
Optionally enter a public article URL and select 'Load URL'; avoid private or paywalled material because loading uses a third-party text fetcher.

risk_flags: Pattern matches are editing prompts, not proof that text was generated by AI.
Public URL loading uses a third-party text fetcher, so private material should be pasted only if the user accepts the tool's browser behavior.
